What is Cache Invalidation?
👉 Cache invalidation = removing or updating stale data from cache when the original data (DB) changes

✅ Simple Idea
DB updated ❌ → Cache still has old data ❌
→ Need to invalidate/update cache ✅


✅ 🔷 Why is it Important?
👉 Biggest problem with cache:

“Cache can become stale (outdated)”


✅ Example
User name = "Bikash" (cached)

User updates name → "Bikash D"

DB updated ✅
Cache still has old value ❌

👉 Wrong response if not invalidated ❌

🔥 ✅ Types of Cache Invalidation (IMPORTANT)

✅ 1. Write-Through Invalidation
💡 Idea
👉 Update cache + DB together

✅ Flow
Update → DB + Cache both updated


✅ Example
updateUser(101, "Bikash D")
→ DB updated
→ Cache updated


✅ Use case

Strong consistency systems (banking)



✅ 2. Cache-Aside (Lazy Invalidation) ⭐ Most Common
💡 Idea
👉 On update → remove cache
👉 Next read → fetch fresh data

✅ Flow
Update → delete cache

Next read:
→ cache miss
→ fetch from DB
→ update cache


✅ Example
updateUser(101)
→ cache.delete(101)

getUser(101)
→ cache miss
→ DB → cache.set()


✅ Why most used?
✅ Simple
✅ Efficient
✅ Used in real systems (Redis)


✅ 3. TTL-based Invalidation
💡 Idea
👉 Cache expires automatically after time

✅ Example
Cache TTL = 10 minutes

After 10 min → removed automatically


✅ Use case

Session data
Temporary data


✅ Limitation

Data may be stale until expiry ❌



✅ 4. Write-Back (Delayed Invalidation)
💡 Idea
👉 Cache updated first, DB later

✅ Risk

Cache and DB can go out of sync



🔥 ✅ Comparison (Easy to Remember)
Cache-Aside → delete cache on update (most common ✅)
Write-Through → update both cache + DB
TTL → expiry-based invalidation
Write-Back → async (risk)


✅ 🔷 Real Example (Amazon Product)
✅ Scenario
User views product → cached ✅

Seller updates price

✅ What to do?
👉 Cache-Aside pattern:
Update DB
Delete cache
Next request → DB → fresh data



✅ ✅ Interview Answer (Perfect)

“Cache invalidation ensures that stale data is removed or updated in cache when the underlying data changes. 
The most common strategy is cache-aside, where cache entries are deleted on updates and refreshed on 
the next read. Other approaches include write-through for strong consistency and TTL-based expiration.”


🔥 🔷 Trick Question (Interview GOLD)
❓ “What is the hardest problem in computer science?”
👉 Answer:

“Cache invalidation and naming things”

✅ Famous answer recruiters LOVE

✅ 🔷 Common Mistakes
❌ Forgetting to invalidate cache
❌ Relying only on TTL
❌ Not handling cache consistency

✅ 🔷 When to Use What

Situation					Strategy
Generalapps					Cache-Aside 
✅Strong consistency			Write-Through
Temporary data				TTL
High performance writes		Write-Back

✅ 🔷 Real System Insight
👉 Most systems use:
Cache-Aside + TTL ✅


✅ 🔥 Final Takeaway
✅ Cache invalidation = keep data fresh
✅ Cache-Aside = most common
✅ Always handle stale data
